sections.h2: Where is the Mahoning County Recorder's office and what hours does it keep?
sections.html:
The office is on the first floor at 120 Market Street, Youngstown, OH 44503. It opens Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the basement self-serve area runs 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The main number is 330-740-2345 and the fax line is 330-740-2347.

Staff will pull a document for you if you can give the recording information, but they cannot search the index on your behalf. A seller who needs to look something up can use one of 13 public computers in the office, or the county's online search. The office also states that it gives no legal advice by phone or at the counter.

The online records system is called Laredo Anywhere. The recorder's page links a basic search and a professional search, and says the web version will also replace the older desktop program on the office's public terminals. A homeowner tracing an old deed or checking whether a mortgage release was ever filed can start there before making a trip downtown, then request a copy using the book and page or instrument number the search returns.

Payment is by check or cash only, and the fee schedule says credit cards are not accepted at this office. Mailed documents come back if the check is for more than the exact recording cost, so confirm the total before you send anything.

sections.h2: How much does the Recorder charge for a deed?
sections.html:
The recorder's schedule says all fees come from the Ohio Revised Code, and it posted a notice that most recording charges rose by $5.00 starting January 1, 2026 under Senate Bill 94. The rates below are the ones printed on the county's page for documents that meet the state formatting rule.

Selected Mahoning County Recorder fees from the county's Schedule of Fees
ItemFee printed by the county
Deed, mortgage, lease or similar record$39.00 for the first two pages, plus $8.00 for each added page or side
Marginal notation (release, assignment, re-recording)Basic fee plus $4.00 for each notation
Plat$0.10 per square inch, minimum $40.00
Certified copy$2.00 per page plus $1.00 for certification
Plain copy$2.00 per page
Military discharge (DD214)No charge
Non-conforming documentExtra $20 on top of the recording fee

For a standard two-page warranty deed, the first line is the one that matters. Longer legal descriptions or attached exhibits add pages and therefore cost.

sections.h2: What must the Auditor approve before a Mahoning County deed can be recorded?
sections.html:
The deed goes to the County Auditor first. Its published checklist says a deed dropped off with anything missing is returned in full for correction. The deed has to show:

  • The marital status of the person signing
  • A tax mailing address for the buyer
  • A legal description and a reference to the prior deed
  • Signatures of the seller and any spouse, with a notary clause and stamp
  • The name and contact details of whoever prepared it
  • A completed state conveyance form, DTE 100 for a sale or DTE 100 EX when no money changes hands

Drop-offs also need a contact name and phone number. The auditor prefers one check per transaction made out to the Mahoning County Treasurer, and blank checks are refused. For a sale, the checklist gives the conveyance fee as $1.00 per $1,000 of price, a permissive fee of $3.00 per $1,000, and a transfer fee of 50 cents per parcel. Exempt transfers pay only the per-parcel fee. Questions go to 330-740-2010, then press 0.

Parcels described in acres, parts of platted lots and outlots take one more stop. They go to the GIS and Tax Map desk in the lobby of 21 West Boardman Street for approval before the auditor will move them. Only after the auditor's stamp does the deed come to the recorder.

sections.h2: What formatting rules can send a deed back or add $20?
sections.html:
Ohio's document standardization law took effect on July 1, 2009, and the recorder applies it to every ordinary deed. A paper that breaks the rules is accepted only with the extra $20. The county lists these requirements:

  • Type at least 10 point in size
  • Paper no smaller than 8 1/2 by 11 and no larger than 8 1/2 by 14
  • Black or blue ink only, with no highlighting
  • One inch margins on the sides and bottom
  • A three inch blank space at the top of page one for the recorder, auditor and engineer stamps
  • A one and a half inch top margin on later pages

The rule does not reach court or tax authority papers, plats, DD214 forms, state and federal documents, or anything signed before the effective date. The recorder's home page also carries a notary fraud alert for anyone handling a notary seal. If a title company prepares the package, it handles most of this for you.

sections.h2: Can a Mahoning County deed be filed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The office accepts electronic recording of deeds, mortgages and mortgage-related documents. It lists three vendors to contact:

  • ePN, 888-325-3365
  • Simplifile, 800-460-5657
  • CSC eRecording Solutions, 866-652-0111

Title companies and lenders usually file this way, which avoids a trip downtown and the check-only rule at the counter. An individual seller doing a quitclaim between relatives will more often walk the paper in. Either path still needs the auditor's stamp on the deed before it can be recorded.

sections.h2: What is Mahoning County like, and who buys homes here?
sections.html:
Mahoning County spans 425 square miles, of which 14 are water, and it borders Trumbull, Portage, Stark and Columbiana counties plus two Pennsylvania counties. It was organized in 1846 and named for the Mahoning River. Youngstown, a steel town for much of the twentieth century, is the seat. The county's 2019 financial report named Mercy Health, the Youngstown school district and the county itself as the three largest employers.

Census QuickFacts puts the 2020 to 2024 median value of owner-occupied homes at $154,700, with 70.3 percent of homes lived in by their owners and a median household income of $56,942. The county recorded 174 building permits in 2025. Population fell from 238,823 in 2010 to 228,614 in 2020. Cities such as Youngstown, Struthers, Campbell and Canfield and villages such as Sebring, Poland and Lowellville all record in the same office.

sections.h2: What should a seller handle before the deed is filed?
sections.html:
Most of the work is a phone call to one office each:

  • Ask the Mahoning County Treasurer at 330-740-2460 what is owed on the parcel
  • Ask a lender for a recorded release of any paid-off mortgage
  • Check with the recorder for liens, since mortgages, judgments and mechanic's liens do not appear on a tax bill
  • Confirm with the county probate court who may sign if the owner has died
  • Match the legal description on your old deed to the auditor's parcel record

A sale for cash goes through the same three stops: auditor, then recorder.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Mahoning County Recorder?
faqs.a: 330-740-2345. The fax number is 330-740-2347, and the office is open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay recording fees with a credit card in Mahoning County?
faqs.a: No. The county's fee schedule says check or cash only and that credit cards are not accepted at the recorder's office. E-filers pay through their vendor.

faqs.q: What did recording fees change to in 2026?
faqs.a: The county's notice says Senate Bill 94 raised most recording fees by $5.00 starting January 1, 2026. The schedule now lists $39.00 for the first two pages of a deed and $8.00 for each added page.

faqs.q: Do I need the Auditor's stamp before I record a deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The auditor reviews the deed and collects the conveyance fees first, and only then does the deed go to the recorder. A deed missing a required item is returned for correction.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for a copy of my military discharge?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's schedule lists military records, including the DD214, as free of charge, citing Ohio Revised Code section 317.24(A).
